neighbours.label: The verb right after a named subject in historical narrative ('Hyde was', 'Roosevelt was', 'food helped'), not in everyday or modern reporting
fire: When the fleet returned from Lisbon in 1589, Drake was blamed by the queen for the failure of the expedition.
Following the fall of the Bastille in 1789, Lafayette was given command of the new national guard in Paris.
After the treaty of Utrecht in 1713, Bolingbroke was soon accused of betraying the allies.
As Venice lost its eastern trade in the fifteenth century, Genoa helped to finance the voyages to the west.
Under the emperor Augustus in the first century, Maecenas was known as the patron of the leading poets.
In the spring of 1863, the Pass was held by Union cavalry until reinforcements arrived from the north.
During the siege of Vienna in 1683, Sobieski was hailed by the defenders as their deliverer.
Late in the reign of Elizabeth, in 1601, Essex was tried for treason and beheaded at the Tower.
quiet: When the bus returned from the mall on Friday, my brother was annoyed by the noise from the back seats.
Following the update of the app last week, the battery was draining faster on my new phone.
After the meeting on Monday morning, our manager was soon asking everyone for the slides.
As the shop lost its weekend trade this year, the owner decided to open a website instead.
At the dentist in the early afternoon, the waiting room was full of parents and small children.
In the spring of this year, the gym was closed for repairs until the new floors arrived.
During the party at my cousin's house, the music was loud enough to wake the neighbours.
Late in the evening on Sunday, my laptop was restarted and the file was gone.

short: verb after subject in history prose
notes: Exploratory probes: 0.27-0.49 in mid-sentence historical clauses, 0.04-0.11 in modern or everyday narration; a sentence-initial name (Petty, 0.06) was weak, so names here are never first.
